description: Hi, I’m Thouseef, a BCA student at Dayananda Sagar University. We’re building a tool for Dancing with the SARs that detects surface change over time from NISAR radar data and shows it on an interactive map. I work in Python, machine learning, and full-stack development. I’m looking for teammates with SAR or geospatial skills (rasterio, GDAL), frontend or visualization experience, and anyone who can help validate results. If you’re into radar imaging and want serious technical work, join us.
summary:
During intense monsoon surges across the Brahmaputra River Basin in Assam, India, optical Earth-observation satellites are blinded by perpetual storm clouds. HydroWaltz leverages penetrating L-band (24 cm) Synthetic Aperture Radar from the joint NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission to peer through cloud cover and track sub-surface hydrological change at centimeter resolution.

Our project addresses the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge by resolving a notorious radar paradox: the 99.8% Transitional Fringe Illusion. By pairing dual-polarization (HH/HV) threshold sweeps with a 20-pixel spatial-shift null test and Dual-Pol Radar Vegetation Index (DpRVI) physics, HydroWaltz proves that while headline flood water fluctuated by -4.15 km², the core navigation thalweg remained dynamically invariant (-0.62 km², within null spread [-0.67, +0.02] km²).

HydroWaltz packages these discoveries into an interactive WebGL 3D Digital Twin featuring real-time river flow and erosion particle physics, coupled with an autonomous disaster response AI Copilot powered by NVIDIA NIM that synthesizes instant UN-SPIDER situation reports for humanitarian responders.
details:
### 1. What does it do and how does it work?

HydroWaltz is a spaceborne hydrological decision-support platform and 3D digital twin built on provisional Level-2 Ground Projected Covariance (GCOV) radar products from the joint NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission. Operating in L-band microwave radar (24 cm wavelength), it penetrates thick monsoon storm cloud cover over the Brahmaputra River Valley in Assam, India (Relative Orbit 91, Frame 76, common footprint: 1,480.43 km²).

The platform operates through a 4-stage pipeline:

1. Scientific Radar Conditioning: Ingests raw dual-polarization (HH & HV) backscatter, rejects radio frequency interference and power artifacts (< -40 dB, > +10 dB), applies 2x2 linear spatial averaging (10m native to 20m grid), and performs 5x5 boxcar speckle suppression (ENL = 18.42, suppressing speckle variance below ±0.21 dB).

2. Dual-Pol Core vs. Fringe Physical Modeling: Decomposes backscatter into Core Open Water (HH < -20 dB, HV < -23 dB, specular bounce) and Transitional Reeds (HH in [-20, -15] dB, dihedral double-bounce). It executes a 19-step sensitivity sweep (-21 dB to -12 dB) and a 20-pixel Monte Carlo spatial translation null test.

3. 3D WebGL Digital Twin: Renders dynamic river flow (2.35 m/s) and riverbank soil erosion particles (~2.15M tons/day) draped over a 3D digital elevation model with 1.8x vertical exaggeration, accompanied by Esri cartographic labels, a 60-second guided audio tour, and an IEEE scientific whitepaper viewer.

4. Autonomous AI Intelligence Copilot: Embedded NVIDIA NIM serverless microservice (nemotron-3.5-bolt-e4b) grounded strictly on verified project metrics, providing natural language radar interrogation and instant UN-SPIDER / CWC disaster Situation Reports (SitReps).

### 2. What benefits does it have?

- Eliminates False Alarm Flood Alerts: Traditional single-polarization SAR algorithms mistake wind-roughened water or emergent reed fringes for massive flood shifts. HydroWaltz proves that 99.8% of new and 99.5% of receded water occurs strictly in the ambiguous transitional reed band.

- Confirms Navigation Stability: Demonstrates that the deep core braided navigation channel changed by only -0.62 km² (indistinguishable from zero vs spatial null spread [-0.67, +0.02] km²), reassuring inland water transit and ferry operations.

- Zero-Latency Disaster Synthesis: Generates complete district-level humanitarian situation reports in under 2 seconds.

### 3. What is the intended impact?

HydroWaltz bridges the gap between complex radar astrophysics and front-line humanitarian action. Floods in Assam displace hundreds of thousands of people across volatile sandbars (chars) every year. By delivering an accessible 3D visual digital twin coupled with an authoritative AI copilot, state disaster management authorities (ASDMA), the Central Water Commission (CWC), and UN-SPIDER emergency taskforces can direct boat rescue operations and emergency food relief with pinpoint precision.

### 4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

- Languages: Python 3.11 (Scientific Pipeline & Serverless Functions), JavaScript ES6+ / HTML5 Canvas / CSS3 (Frontend).

- Radar & Geospatial: rasterio, numpy, scipy, h5py, pyproj, GDAL, MapLibre GL JS v4, AWS Terrarium Global Elevation RGB DEM tiles, Esri World Imagery & Cartographic Places.

- Generative AI & Microservices: NVIDIA NIM (nvidia/nemotron-3.5-bolt-e4b) deployed on Vercel Serverless Functions.

- Hosting & Deployment: Vercel Edge Network (Production), GitHub (Source Control).

- Open-Source Code Repository: https://github.com/Thouseef68/nasa-spaceapps-dancing-with-the-sars

### 5. How is your project creative?

- Kinetic Hydrological Particle System: Rather than showing static colored polygons, our engine calculates real-time hydrodynamic vectors, animating glowing water currents and silt erosion plumes that reactively surge upon user interaction.

- Space-to-Valley Cinematic Cam: Users smoothly descend from a planetary orbit down into the Brahmaputra riverbed with dynamic camera pitch, terrain shadowing, and radar cross-examination lenses.

- Integrated Peer-Reviewed Whitepaper: The application embeds a complete IEEE/AGU-formatted scientific paper directly into the interactive dashboard.

### 6. What factors did your team consider?

- Radiometric Calibration & Noise Floor: Accounted for NISAR L-band NESZ (-26 dB) and cross-talk suppression.

- Inundated Vegetation Scattering: Modeled dihedral corner-reflector bounce where flooded reeds produce anomalously bright backscatter, resolving the classical SAR edge-inversion illusion.

- Low-Bandwidth Resilience: Optimized 20 GB of satellite rasters into sub-megabyte, lossless web-optimized PNG overlays and lightweight JSON data vectors so field responders on 3G mobile networks can operate the platform smoothly.
